Stir-fried Tofu and Mixed Vegetables

Served at: Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana)

Serves 4-6Prep 25 minCook 15 min

This vibrant and wholesome stir-fry is a perfect offering for the Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana), also known as Hungry Ghost Festival. Adhering to the festival's vegetarian principles, it features a medley of fresh vegetables and protein-rich tofu, symbolizing purity and respect for all living beings. It's a nourishing dish often prepared for family gatherings and as an offering to ancestors during this time of remembrance.

Ingredients

  • 1 block (14-16 ounces / 400-450g) firm or extra-firm tofu
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) soy sauce, divided
  • 1 tablespoon (8g) cornstarch
  • 1 tablespoon (15ml) sesame oil
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) vegetable oil, divided
  • 1 medium onion (about 6 ounces / 170g), sliced
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 inch (2.5cm) fresh ginger, grated
  • 1 cup (150g) broccoli florets
  • 1 cup (150g) sliced carrots
  • 1 cup (100g) sliced bell peppers (any color)
  • 1 cup (70g) snap peas or snow peas
  • 1/2 cup (60g) sliced mushrooms (shiitake or cremini)
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) vegetable broth or water
  • 1 tablespoon (15ml) vegetarian oyster sauce or additional soy sauce
  • 1 teaspoon (4g) sugar
  • Cooked rice, for serving

Method

  1. Press the tofu to remove excess water: wrap it in paper towels or a clean cloth and place a heavy object on top for at least 15-20 minutes.
  2. Cut the pressed tofu into 1-inch (2.5cm) cubes.
  3. In a medium bowl, gently toss the tofu cubes with 1 tablespoon (15ml) soy sauce and cornstarch until evenly coated.
  4. Heat 1 tablespoon (15ml) vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
  5. Add the tofu and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and slightly crispy on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove tofu from the skillet and set aside.
  6. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon (15ml) vegetable oil to the skillet. Add the sliced onion and cook until softened, about 2-3 minutes.
  7. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
  8. Add the broccoli florets and sliced carrots, stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
  9. Add the bell peppers, snap peas, and mushrooms, and stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes.
  10. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tablespoon (15ml) soy sauce, vegetable broth, vegetarian oyster sauce (or additional soy sauce), and sugar.
  11. Pour the sauce mixture into the skillet with the vegetables. Bring to a simmer and cook for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
  12. Return the cooked tofu to the skillet and gently toss to combine with the vegetables and sauce.
  13. Drizzle with sesame oil, stir briefly, and serve immediately over steamed rice.

Tips

  • Feel free to customize the vegetables based on seasonal availability or preference; bok choy, baby corn, or water chestnuts are great additions.
  • For a spicier kick, add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the garlic and ginger.
  • Ensure your wok or skillet is hot enough before adding ingredients to achieve a good stir-fry texture.
